outcome.answer:
For distributional RL in chaotic dynamical systems, Paper [1] directly argues that chaotic dynamics make scalar-value RL objectives ill-conditioned due to exponential sensitivity to initial conditions, while the return distribution evolves more regularly. It shows that, under mild statistical stability assumptions, aligning distributional RL with the 1-Wasserstein metric yields a smoother distributional Bellman objective and better-conditioned learning. 

If you instead mean “chaos” through model/forecast multiplicity, Paper [3] studies how predictive equivalence (Rashomon sets) changes with prediction horizon under chaos, providing Lyapunov-weighted metrics and horizon-constrained selection algorithms. These are forecasting/selection results rather than a distributional RL mechanism.

Other supplied works use distributional or related generative modeling tools but do not specifically target distributional RL chaotic dynamics: Paper [2] focuses on extracting dynamic-programming structure from distributional RL learning dynamics in general; Papers [7] and [6] propose distributional RL methods for other settings; Paper [5] studies extrapolation of global chaotic dynamics using transformers; Paper [9] develops generative joint probability models for chaotic forecasting; Paper [4] is distributionally robust RL theory; and Paper [10] is distributional control for jump-diffusion games.
